intro: A fairly quiet Friday. The main themes are Google pulling more shopping into Search and Gemini, Amazon turning Kindle Unlimited into Kindle+ with audiobooks, and fresh data showing AI answers start shopping journeys but rarely finish them. Reddit feeds were mostly rate-limited today, so Reddit coverage is thin. There were no Geniuslink, geni.us or Booklinker mentions. Deal posts, stock pages and off-topic matches were left out.

must_reads.title: Google Rolls Out Universal Cart Across Search and Gemini in the US
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Google now lets US shoppers save products, get price alerts, find promo codes and check out from Search and Gemini. The more the buying journey stays inside Google, the fewer chances a shopper has to click through a creator's or publisher's link to the retailer.

must_reads.title: Amazon Renames Kindle Unlimited "Kindle+" and Adds Audiobooks, Including AI-Voiced Titles, at the Same Price
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Amazon has renamed Kindle Unlimited to Kindle+ and added audiobooks, including AI-voiced ones, in the US at the same price. Authors who link to their books will want to check which format and store page their readers land on now that one subscription covers both.

must_reads.title: Google AI Overviews reach 88% of commercial searches as AI clicks stay thin
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Semrush finds Google's AI answers now appear on 88% of tracked shopping-type searches, while other studies put ChatGPT traffic at under 1% of Google's organic traffic. AI answers are taking up more of the page, but they still send very few clicks out, so links in creator content stay an important route to the sale.

must_reads.title: AI boosts discovery but reviews still seal the deal, new research shows
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: A Feedvisor survey finds 16% of shoppers start looking for products in ChatGPT, but only 9% go there to buy and just 5% buy straight away. People still hop to Google, Amazon and retailer sites to compare, which is exactly the moment a link that sends them to the right store matters.

must_reads.title: From influence to checkout: Is performance the next test for creator marketing?
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Creator marketing in India is moving from paying for reach to paying per sale or click, with YouTube Shopping and Amazon leading the way. When creators are paid on results, tracking every click to the right store becomes part of how they get paid.

items.title: Attribution matters more once creator spend turns double-digit, says Nidhi Thakkar of Amazon
items.summary: Amazon India's Nidhi Thakkar says YouTube Shopping and Pinterest links are shrinking the gap between discovery and purchase, and that measuring creator sales gets harder as budgets grow.
